newsitem.title: USA: Secondhand smoke jury loses two alternates.
newsitem.headline: Secondhand smoke jury loses two alternates.

text.p: Two of the alternates selected for the jury that will hear a landmark secondhand smoke case against the tobacco industry were dismissed Thursday, dropping the number of alternates available for the trial to eight.
"We'll excuse both of those people," Dade County Circuit Judge Robert Kaye said during a pre-trial hearing in Norma Broin vs. Philip Morris Cos Inc.
The panel of six jurors and 10 alternates was sworn in Wednesday after a painstaking selection process that began June 2.

Attorneys for the tobacco industry and the plaintiffs agreed to the dismissal of the two alternates -- a man who said he had extensive business travel in Latin America, and a woman whose husband recently sued her for divorce.
Thousands of non-smoking flight attendants are suing cigarette makers for $5 billion, seeking redress for illnesses that they allege are linked to breathing second-hand smoke on U.S.-based airliners.
It will be the first second-hand smoke case and first class action against the tobacco industry to go to trial.
Opening arguments are expected to begin July 14.
